newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-METS' BOBBY JONES BEATS PIRATES FOR 12TH WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-METS' BOBBY JONES BEATS PIRATES FOR 12TH WIN.

text.p: Bobby Jones became the first 12-game winner in the majors and rookie Jason Hardtke drove in the game's only run as the New York Mets edged the Pittsburgh Pirates 1-0 Friday.

Jones (12-3) bounced back from his first loss in more than seven weeks, to the Boston Red Sox, by limiting the Pirates to six singles over 8 2/3 innings. He walked two and struck out eight in improving to 4-1 lifetime against Pittsburgh.

"I looked back at the Boston game and saw what got me in trouble," Jones said. "I made some adjustments, moved the ball around, kept it low and threw strikes. My curveball was as good as it has been."
"He pitched one of his best games of the year tonight," said Mets manager Bobby Valentine.

In 15 starts this season, Jones has gone at least eight innings nine times. He has allowed one run or less seven times and lowered his earned run average from 2.49 to 2.29, third best in the National League. His 12 wins match his career high, achieved in 1994 and last year.

Jones got the first two outs in the ninth but surrendered a single to Mark Smith. John Franco, who surrendered a game-tying three-run homer Thursday, got Jose Guillen on a high chopper up the middle to notch his 18th save.
Franco's save was the 341st of his career, tying Rollie Fingers for fourth on the all-time list.
Hardtke, who drove in the winning run in the ninth Thursday, laced a line drive to left-centre in the sixth to score Butch Huskey.
"I just got up in a good spot again," Hardtke said.
Steve Cooke (5-9) allowed just one run and seven hits in six innings. He has lost three straight decisions.

In Houston, Derek Bell's three-run homer, his first in more than five weeks, capped a four-run third inning and Darryl Kile won for the seventh time in eight decisions as the Astros handed the Chicago Cubs their third straight loss, 7-3.
Houston's Luis Gonzalez tied Art Howe's club record (1981) by extending his hitting streak to 23 games.
"I'm not thinking about the streak. I just want to win these games within our division," said Gonzalez, a former Cub.
Kevin Orie drove in all three runs for Chicago.

In San Francisco, pinch-hitter Nelson Liriano's two-run double in the top of the 10th highlighted a four-run outburst as the Los Angeles Dodgers recovered from blowing a seven-run lead to defeat the Giants 11-7.

Todd Zeile singled off reliever Doug Henry (2-3) and one out later stole second. Walks to Eric Karros and Raul Mondesi loaded the bases and with Liriano at-bat, a passed ball by catcher Marcus Jensen allowed Zeile to score the go-ahead run.
Liriano then doubled down the line in right to plate Karros and Mondesi. Wilton Guerrero added an RBI single.
Henry surrendered four runs and three hits in two-thirds of an inning.

San Francisco trailed 7-6 in the bottom of the ninth but Barry Bonds' second homer of the game, a solo shot off Los Angeles closer Todd Worrell, sent the game into extra innings. Worrell (1-1) got the win, anyway.
Karim Garcia hit his first career homer, a three-run blast, and Greg Gagne added a solo shot for the Dodgers, who won for the third time in their last four games.
Mark Lewis hit a two-run homer and J.T. Snow added a solo homer for San Francisco, which had its five-game winning streak snapped.
In Montreal, Alex Fernandez pitched a three-hitter and Charles Johnson had a homer in the fifth and an RBI triple in the seventh as the Florida Marlins beat the Expos 2-1.
The loss snapped a nine-game home winning streak for the Expos, who have won 11 of their last 13 overall.

Fernandez (7-6) allowed just an RBI double to Chris Widger in the second with three walks and four strikeouts in his third complete game of the year. The righty retired the final 16 batters and did not allow a hit after the second inning.

In Philadelphia, Tom Glavine pitched a seven-hitter for his third complete game of the season and Andruw Jones had a two-run double in a four-run sixth inning as the Atlanta Braves handed the Phillies their sixth straight loss, 4-1.
Glavine (7-4), who won for the first time in three starts, has allowed only one earned run in his last 18 innings.
Atlanta played without starters Kenny Lofton (strained groin), Michael Tucker (pulled muscle in right side) and Javier Lopez (bruised left knee).
Mark Leiter (4-8) is winless in his last six starts.
In San Diego, Archi Cianfrocco's run-scoring double snapped an eighth-inning tie as the Padres stopped a five-game losing streak with a 5-2 win over the Colorado Rockies.
Andy Ashby (3-3) allowed two runs and nine hits in eight innings for the first win by a San Diego starter since Will Cunnane also beat Colorado on June 4.
In St Louis, Deion Sanders and Pokey Reese hit solo homers and Kent Mercker (5-5) allowed just two runs over six innings as the Cincinnati Reds handed the Cardinals their fifth straight loss, 4-2.
Cincinnati won for the ninth time in 13 games.
